text:
A: Hiya, er, can you hear us?
B: Yeah. Hi. Gareth.
A: Craig. Hartlepool.
B: Basingstoke.
A: Right, aye. *(pause)* Yeah... er. Is that your fourth one?
B: Yeah. Last one, I think.
A: Same. I'm getting the hang of it now, like. First one I was sat here sweating.
B: *(laughs)* Yeah. Bit odd, talking to a screen.
A: Aye. Is that a Saints magnet I can see on your fridge?
B: Yeah. Fixtures. You're Hartlepool, then? Saw the scarf.
A: Aye, Pools. Long-suffering. We've been up and down more than a lift. How are Saints doing?
B: Er, sort of up and down too. Lost Saturday. Should've won it, we had loads of the ball.
A: That's always the way, isn't it. You have all the ball and then they nick one off a corner.
B: Exactly that, yeah. Off a corner.
A: Do you go much?
B: Couple of times a season. With my lad, Callum. He's fifteen.
A: Ah, that's nice, that. I used to go with me dad every home game. He's gone now, so. You want to keep doing that with him, you know.
B: Yeah. *(pause)* Yeah, I should do more of it. My dad's not well at the minute, actually. My sister does most of it. I sort of leave her to it, which isn't great.
A: Ah, sorry, mate. It's hard when you've got kids and work and that.
B: Yeah. No excuse really.
A: Nah, you're doing your best, like. Er, have you got a daughter as well, then? Only, Gemma said, I think, someone had an Ellie.
B: Yeah, Ellie. Twelve.
A: No way! Mine's Ellie and all. Nine. That's her on the wall.
B: *(laughs)* Gemma said that to me, yeah. Popular name.
A: Must've been the year for it. Is she a handful?
B: Er, she's alright. She runs the house, sort of. I'm on my own with them most of the week, their mum's in Reading. So she tells me what I've forgotten.
A: Aye, I'm divorced. Four year now. Nobody's fault really, we just sort of drifted. I still get on with her for Ellie's sake. I have her every other weekend, she sleeps in the box room at me mam's. I'm back at me mam's, like. Thirty-five. It's a bit daft, but there you go.
B: Doesn't sound daft. *(pause)* We're about eighteen months in. Not divorced, just separated. Nobody's done the paperwork.
A: Ah, right. Paperwork's the worst bit, honestly. Did me head in.
B: Yeah. I'm bad at paperwork anyway. Probably why it's not done.
A: *(laughs)* Fair enough. What do you do, then?
B: Structural engineer. Warehouses, retail units.
A: Oh, aye? I'm a brickie. Well, was. Done me back. So I've probably built the walls you've drawn, like.
B: *(laughs)* Probably, yeah. Blockwork infill on a portal frame, that's half my drawings.
A: That's half me working life, that. Laying blocks in the rain off some drawing an engineer did in a warm office.
B: Sorry about that.
A: Nah, you're alright. I'm thinking of going for site supervisor, maybe. If me back holds up.
B: You'd get on alright. Good supervisors are hard to find. Most of the ones I deal with just shout.
A: Aye, I'm not a shouter. Is it—
